1#main: That one must write it for its sake, and the law of correcting letters and their adornment. In it are 7 seifim. The scribe must say when he begins to write this book: "I am writing for the sake of the sanctity of a Sefer Torah"—and this suffices for the entire book.
2#main: He must have another book before him from which he copies, for it is forbidden to write even one letter not from a written text; and he must read each word aloud before writing it.
3#main: He should write a fair, straight script; and if he wrote aleph-lamed together like this: ﭏ—it is not valid.
4#main: Each letter must be surrounded by hide on all four sides, so it not stick to its fellow; rather there should be between them like a hair's breadth. And they should not be separated greatly from one another so one word not appear as two. And there should be between word and word the full width of a small letter. And one should not bring them too close so two words not appear as one. And if he changed—distanced the letters until the word appears as two, or brought two words close until they appear as one—it is invalid.
5#main: Care must be taken that the form of no letter be impaired until it is not recognizable, or similar to another letter—whether in the main writing, whether in a tear, whether in a hole pierced in it, or in smudging. (And he may take ink from a written letter when he needs ink (Hagahos Maimoniyos chapter 2), or when he wishes to roll the book) (Rosh, general rule 3).
6#main: One must be careful about correcting letters and their adornment as explained at length in the laws of tefillin, siman 32 and siman 36.
7#main: A book with vowel points is invalid—even if the pointing was removed from it. And likewise a book that has punctuation of verses is invalid. {Rama: And specifically when he made the break with ink; but if he left air between the verses, as long as there is not the measure of a valid parashah, it is valid (responsum of the Rivash). And a Sefer Torah in which letters are mixed up as in a get is not invalid, but l'chatchila one should not do so (there, siman 146).}
